"Instead of burning or shredding the clippings from your winter garden maintenance, consider transforming them into a dead hedge. This creative solution serves multiple purposes: it functions as an excellent windbreak, provides a sanctuary for local wildlife, and helps separate different sections of your garden. To build one, simply drive stakes or old fence posts into the ground in two parallel rows, approximately 50 centimeters apart, and then layer your pruned material between them, placing the thicker branches at the bottom. Over time, the material will naturally compress and settle.

If you feel disappointed about your Christmas gifts, you might want to brighten your mood by pre-ordering 'The Book of Seeds' by Paul Smith, who previously led Kew's Millennium Seed Bank. Available from Ivy Press at £30 and releasing in February, this gorgeous book explores 600 of the planet's most extraordinary and visually stunning seed species.

For a spectacular winter garden display, consider planting winter-flowering clematis in a warm, protected location. Varieties such as 'Advent Bells,' C. cirrhosa var. balearica, and 'Jingle Bells' offer beautiful blooms ranging from creamy scented flowers with maroon markings to pure white blossoms throughout the winter months."
